_note: Track C alert policy. Draft values: every entry has pharmacist_approved=false until the pharmacist session (PS_ANALYSIS section 4, Q4/Q6/Q9). Do not present as clinical limits.

alert_budget.note: Extra routine interrupts are shown as 'inform' (budget_demoted). Types in never_demote (contraindicated interactions, banned FDCs, kidney 'avoid', weekly-read-as-daily, high-risk stacks) are never demoted and do not use up the budget. The average-per-Rx target of <=1 is measured by eval/.

ddi_tiers.source: DDInter 2.0 severity mapped to our tiers; no pair is interrupt until the pharmacist names it (Q6)

refill.source: Team setting: a repeat of the same medicine by the same doctor within a week of the supply ending is read as a refill. Pharmacist to set the real number.

burden_scales.label: Anticholinergic burden
burden_scales.source: Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden scale, 2012 update (Aging Brain Care, Indiana University). Starter subset of the published list; scores to be checked against the original table. A total of 3 or more is the usual cut-off.

burden_scales.label: Three or more CNS-active medicines
burden_scales.source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, drug-drug interactions: avoid three or more CNS-active drugs (falls, fractures). One point per ingredient in these classes; list of classes to confirm with the pharmacist.

aware._note: WHO AWaRe antibiotic groups. Reserve = last-resort, only for infections with few options; Watch = higher resistance potential, a stewardship target; Access = first choice. Only systemic lines. Clavulanic acid, sulbactam and tazobactam are partners, not scored on their own.
aware.label: WHO AWaRe classification 2023
aware.version: WHO AWaRe classification 2023, transcribed by hand for the antibiotics common in India; drugs I was not sure of are left out, not guessed

stack_rules.label: ACE inhibitor/ARB + diuretic + NSAID
stack_rules.reason: {names} together: a blood-pressure drug acting on the kidney, a diuretic and an NSAID (the 'triple whammy') raise the risk of acute kidney injury (age {age}, CrCl {crcl} mL/min). Pharmacist to review before dispensing.
stack_rules.source: Lapi F et al., BMJ 2013;346:e8525 (triple combination and acute kidney injury).

stack_rules.label: Anticoagulant + NSAID
stack_rules.reason: {names} together: an anticoagulant with an NSAID markedly raises the risk of serious bleeding. Pharmacist to review before dispensing.
stack_rules.source: Anticoagulant and NSAID product labelling; AGS Beers Criteria 2023 (interactions to avoid).

stack_rules.label: Two antiplatelets + NSAID
stack_rules.reason: {names} together: two antiplatelet drugs plus an NSAID raise the risk of stomach and other serious bleeding. Pharmacist to review before dispensing.

stack_rules.label: Two NSAIDs in a high-risk patient
stack_rules.reason: {names}: two NSAIDs at once add stomach-bleeding and kidney risk without more pain relief (age {age}, CrCl {crcl} mL/min). Pharmacist to review.
stack_rules.source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023; NSAID product labelling. Stops at age 65+, CrCl below 60 or with an anticoagulant/antiplatelet.

stack_rules.label: Several potassium-raising drugs
stack_rules.reason: {names}: each raises blood potassium; together high potassium is likely, more so with weak kidneys (CrCl {crcl} mL/min). Pharmacist to review.
stack_rules.source: Product labelling; AGS Beers Criteria 2023 (interactions to avoid).

stack_rules.label: SSRI/SNRI + tramadol or dextromethorphan
stack_rules.reason: {names}: together they raise the risk of serotonin syndrome (and seizures with tramadol); cough syrups and painkillers can hide the second drug. Pharmacist to review.
stack_rules.source: Product labelling (tramadol, dextromethorphan, SSRIs). tier to confirm

stack_rules.label: Several QT-prolonging drugs
stack_rules.reason: {names}: each can prolong the QT interval; together the risk of a dangerous heart rhythm rises (age {age}). Pharmacist to review.
stack_rules.source: Drug list transcribed from the CredibleMeds 'known risk of TdP' category; to verify against the registered QTdrugs list (non-commercial use).
